newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to open tender for Gdanski.
newsitem.headline: Poland to open tender for Gdanski.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry, holding nearly 40 percent of shares in Bank Gdanski SA, will open a tender a stake in the bank in December, deputy Finance Minister Ryszard Pazura said on Monday.
"We will launch a tender for Gdanski shares in December," Pazura told a news briefing.
Pazura said the ministry would soon set up a special commission that would establish criteria for the tender. He said it was too early to say how big a stake would be offered.

By law, the ministry can offer up to 34.9 percent of shares in the bank, as five percent has been put aside for a government programme compensating former owners of property confiscated under communism.

Last month, HSBC Investment Bank released the treasury from a lockup agreement linked with its issue of Gdanski global depositary receipts, which prevented the state from selling further shares in the bank until late December.
The Bank of New York holds 19.5 percent of Gdanski's GDRs, equivalent to 19.5 percent of its shares.
Poland's bank BIG SA and its subsidiaries have about 31 percent and small investors on the Warsaw bourse hold the rest.
Gdanski has 25 percent of its shares traded in GDRs on the London bourse, 19.5 percent of which is held by the Bank of New York.
